detailed_review.score_reasoning: One spine applied twice, and the linter was excluded from both sums. score_before = 10 - (F1 2 + F2 1 + F3 1 + F4 1 + F5 1 + F6 0.5 + F7 0.5 + F8 0.5) = 10 - 7.5 = 2.5, floored to 2. The 2 on F1 is the skill's flat detraction for type-mixture; the four 1s are a source-contradicted claim (F2), an unfollowable pointer (F3), an example that demonstrates nothing on a page about phrasing (F4) and a terminology collision with a second meaning live on the same page (F5); the three 0.5s are consistency nits (F6, F7, F8). score_after = 10 - (F1 2 + F2 1 + F3 1 + F8 0.5 + F9 0.5) = 10 - 5.0 = 5.0, floored to 5, so the delta is +3 and the verdict is FAIL. Read the 5 carefully before acting on it: 3.5 of the 5.0 open penalty is structural work the dispatch explicitly assigned elsewhere (F1 and F8 to T8, F2 to T28), and 1.0 is a corpus-wide question about an unpublished document that touches two other canonical pages. The two corrections T3 was dispatched to make are both correct and neither appears in remaining[]. This score grades the page as it stands, which is what the contract asks for; it is not a verdict on the T3 author pass.
detailed_review.what_worked: The two T3 corrections landed and I could not fault either. Line 112 now reads "the install root; the default is computed", which removes the drive literal without duplicating the 44-word rule the same page already states fifty lines down, and "the install root" is the term the prose establishes two lines above and the term wiki/style-guide.md:35 makes canonical. The stale 8 GB example is gone, the dated framing survives at both sites as the settled remedy required, and no machine class is named or implied anywhere in the rewritten passage: the take-turns wording is now a conditional attached to coexistence, not to a size. The author's contested choice, re-anchoring on the refusal case rather than dropping the example, was the right call and is now earned. It was not earned as delivered, which is F4: the paragraph described the message's four ingredients and said "the refusal ... says the machine cannot run Hearth", which is circular, and on a section whose entire argument is about wording it showed no wording. The fix names what actually carries the principle, that the message leads with what the outcome means and only then gives the arithmetic, and sends the reader to wiki/install-macos.md:32-34, where the shipped sentence is already published in full. Pointing rather than copying is deliberate: T3 exists because a computed figure was duplicated onto a second page and went stale there, and a decision record is the last page that should hold a number. F5 removed a genuine ambiguity, since "whether the brain and the voice can be resident at the same time" sat eleven lines from a heading that uses "brain" for something else entirely. F6 and F7 are small and now consistent with the corpus.
detailed_review.what_holds_score_down: F1 is most of it. The page is a decision record for its first half and a build specification for its second: "### The direction" reproduces an authored skill document in imperative mood, the two tool sections are parameter catalogs, and beat three is a script with the lines to say. The reader-visible symptom is that four other pages link here for "the full walkthrough", so a reader arriving from wiki/installing.md:146 is promised a walkthrough and handed a rationale. F9 is the same fault at the top of the page: the abstract names a topic instead of stating a decision, where the corpus model at wiki/backend/native-runtime.md:18-20 gives the decision, the exclusion and the date in three lines. F2 is a claim the source tree contradicts, still on the page and now visible in the score, which is the honest place for it while T28 is open. F3 sends a reader to "the portability ledger, section 8" twice; the only such document is wiki/raw/portability-ledger.md, and raw/ never reaches a published reader. The linter cannot catch that one, because the page names the document in English rather than linking a raw/ path, and neither can it catch the same pattern at wiki/backend/build-pipeline.md:181 and wiki/backend/packaging-options.md:193. F8 is minor and waits on the restructure. Also open and not charged: the page still quotes the take-turns warning as live product behavior while crates/hearth-probe/tests/plan_fixtures.rs:40-41 says the orchestration behind it may never need building, and no documented machine class reaches it. That is an engineering question, not a writing defect, so it carries no detraction, but if the branch is retired in code this record should say so rather than outliving it.

detailed_review.not_findings: Recorded so a later pass does not re-litigate them. The linter owns and I did not report: reader-drift on "the user" (many sites on this page), long paragraphs, long sections, bold-lead blocks, sentence case, em dashes, emojis, its own British word list, dead links and frontmatter. I could not run it in this session and say so at the top of this artifact. Beyond that: no figure was requested, although the page describes the plan screen and the voice-check screen, because wiki/installing.md:88 and :137 already carry pending capture orders for both surfaces, and a second work order for the same screenshot is churn. The line 112 annotation was tested and passed; asking it to restate the computed rule would duplicate a fact that is already on the page and is exactly the failure mode this task was opened to fix. The prose references to tasks/*.md at line 48 are a corpus-wide habit shared with wiki/releasing.md:179 and wiki/backend/tool-catalog.md:118, not a defect of this page. No heading rename was made anywhere, and no page in wiki/ links to a first-run.md anchor, so the restructure is free to rename.
